text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A plan put to the Federal Government by States and Territories has proposed a cut-off date of January 1, 2000, be imposed on native title claims. The plan also advises legislation to extinguish native title on pastoral leases be rushed through Parliament by April. The discussion paper was developed after a meeting between State and Territory heads and Prime Minister John Howard. Page 1.

A competitiveness study prepared by consultants Cutler & Co for the Government's Information Industries Task Force claims Australia is 'entirely uncompetitive' with Asia in international technology markets and forecasts that without radical government acton Australia's trade imbalance in information technology and telecommunications will more than double to A$30 billion by 2005. Page 1.

Western Australian Justice Michael Murray yesterday sentenced failed tycoon Alan Bond to a maximum of four years' jail on two counts of acting dishonestly as a company director of Bell Resources, which he defrauded of more than A$1 billion. Bond will effectivey be doing time at a rate of one day for every A$2 million involved in the theft. Page 1.

ACTU Secretary Bill Kelty has give assurance that other unions would not seek to flow-on an 11 per cent increase in award wages negotiated between the Transport Workers Union and trucking employer. Kelty told the Australian Industrial Relations Commission that leaders of all major unions had agreed against seeking wage rises based on the trucking industry agreement. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Howard Government's first annual Trade Outcomes and Objectives statement reveals Trade Minister Tim Fischer plans to tackle unfair trade barriers and enforce world trade rules targeting the United States and key Asian countries. The statement states that Australia's trade policies must aim to boost economic growth, jobs and living conditions in this country. Page 1.

Despite being sentenced yesterday to four years jail for defrauding Bell Resources of over A$1 billion, failed tycoon Alan Bond will be free in just over two years. With parole and remission the 58-year-old will only serve 20 months time on top of an existing prison term for fraud. Page 1.

Federal Liberal backbencher Andrew Thomspon has demanded the Federal Government change air traffic plans which would cut the number of people affected by aircraft noise but increase high-level disturbance in areas to the south, east and west of Sydney. Th changes are part of a new strategy suggested by an Airservices Australia report. Page 3.

New measures announced by Federal Treasurer Peter Costello will see politicians' superannuation payouts slashed in a move to implement the Budget tax on the super of high-income earners. Politicians will now face the highest rate of tax on their super payouts, although their benefits remain more generous than for ordinary workers. Page 2.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Federal Transport Minister John Sharp yesterday released a report prepared by Airservices Australia recommending major changes to the long-term operation of Sydney Airport. The changes include the modification of flight paths over Sydney to spread aircraft noise over more suburbs and reduce the number of chronically effected residents. Page 1.

It has been revealed Prime Minister John Howard knew late last year that Australian Federal Police were investigating allegations of parliamentary office entitlement misuse by Senator Bob Woods but had since forgotten the fact. The revelation contradicts Howard's statement on A Current Affair on Tuesday in which he claims he only knew of the matter 10 days earlier. Page 1.

After being sentenced yesterday to four years imprisonment for committing Australia's largest corporate fraud, failed business tycoon Alan Bond was talking of his comeback. When Bond is released from prison - possibly as early as 1999 - he intends to re-enter the business world, claiming his forte is in the realm of property and resources. Page 1.

Former live-in partner of Senator Bob Woods, Roxanne Cameron has applied for an apprehended violence order against him and is considering launching defamation proceedings as well. Cameron says she has never harassed anyone, contrary to claims made by Senaor Woods. Page 2.
THE AGE

Prime Minister John Howard has admitted knowing about an inquiry into allegations of misuse of parliamentary expense accounts by Senator Bob Woods as early as last year. Howard claimed he was only told 10 days ago about the Australian Federal Police Inqury but has now admitted that he did know about the inquiry, but had forgotten. Page 1.

Failed business tycoon Alan Bond yesterday received a four year jail term for two counts of acting dishonestly as a company director, to be added to the jail sentence he is already serving for fraud. Shortly after sentencing Bond released a statement outlining his future plans and direction, which he believes will be in the business world. Page 1.

Melbourne temperature of 40.9 degrees yesterday was the hottest February 5 on record for the city. The heatwave is expected to continue until a cool change arrives on Sunday. A total fire ban has not been issued although this situation will be reviewed during the day. Page 1.

Communications Minister Richard Alston yesterday answered questions in the Senate about a Cabinet submission of 2 July last year which outlined proposals to cut ABC funding by either A$55 million or A$125 million. Alston said he could not remember if he had signed the submission which admitted on its front page that its options for ABC funding cuts would breach election promises. Page 3.
